correctness.rationale: The extension is constant-preserving precisely when signed weights sum to one; the operator norm is max(1,Phi(w)/R). Testing distance cones gives Phi>=max_i Dw_i>=average_i Dw_i=c_n; uniform weights attain c_n. Equality forces Dw=c_n 1, and cyclic second differences give 2w_i=w_(i+m)+w_(i+m+1) for odd n=2m+1, hence uniformity via a maximum principle and gcd(m,2m+1)=1. For even n=2m they force antipodal equality; increasing the value of a distance-cone potential at the antipode of a negative coefficient by 1 preserves graph-edge Lipschitz constraints and contradicts optimality. Conversely any nonnegative antipodal pair weights have constant distance mean m/2 and attain Phi=c_n. Metric iff R>=diam/2, optimizer set full-dimensional and compact for R>c_n by continuity and finite-dimensional norm coercivity. This is a complete analytic proof, not a claim based on finite integer dual enumeration n<=12.
